chapter: Picnics, wagon advertising and saloon work
title: Advertising a Gretna dance by wagon
summary: He explains why Jack Carey's band advertised dances across the river in Gretna and what the hand-painted signs said.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: One other question to interrupt. Come Clean Hall, was that across the river or over here?
That was across the river in Gretna.
Was it usual to come here to advertise a dance that took place in Gretna? Did you get offered?
Well, you see, Jack Carey, he was well-liked on this side of the river, and he'd draw the crowd.
He'd draw across the river.
He made our biggest advertising in New Orleans.
I see.
Well, we'd make about five or six blocks in Gretna.

Well, I guess there were signs on the side of the wagon. Oh, sure. That's right. What would it say, for example? I mean, how would it read, you know, for that dance, you know? What would the sign say?

Well, sign would say, on Monday, the date, dance given by the Wolves Club. They had a Wolves Forest Club over the river. Oh, yeah. Which they had a hall, too. They called a Wolves Forest. But these boys, they would throw a dance often at the Come Clean Hall. I see. Was that hand-painted design or printed or? Oh, yeah, hand-painted. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Crescent.
